title: Research at Netgroup
description: This page contains information related to the research activities in the Networking Group (NetGroup). The main research topics are related to:

topics.name: Network security analysis and verification
topics.description: We develop formal and automated techniques to analyze, verify, and validate the security of networked systems. Research includes vulnerability analysis, policy verification, firewall analysis, protocol verification, traffic monitoring, and methods for ensuring the correctness of security configurations.

topics.name: Connected Cooperative and Automated Mobility
topics.description: We research communication technologies for connected and automated vehicles, focusing on V2X communications, cooperative driving, intelligent transportation systems, and ETSI ITS standards. Our work includes low-latency networking, vehicular applications, and reliable communication protocols for future mobility services.

topics.name: Network software engineering
topics.description: We develop software engineering methodologies, programming abstractions, and development frameworks for building reliable, maintainable, and high-performance networked systems. Our research includes network programmability (e.g., P4-based in-network processing), reusable software components, verification-aware development, and tools that simplify the implementation of modern network functions.

topics.name: AI/ML for networks
topics.description: We apply artificial intelligence and machine learning to improve network management, operation, and security. Research topics include network automation via LLMs, traffic engineering, anomaly detection, intent-based management, federated learning, reinforcement learning, and large language models for autonomous network operations.

topics.name: Networking for AI
topics.description: We investigate networking systems and protocols that enable efficient distributed AI training and inference. Our work focuses on communication-efficient AI, in-network computing, high-performance data movement, edge AI infrastructures, and scalable architectures supporting AI workloads across cloud and edge environments.

topics.name: 5G/6G Networks
topics.description: We investigate next-generation mobile network architectures, protocols, and services. Research spans network slicing, Open RAN, edge-native mobile systems, AI-native network management, ultra-low latency communications, and resource optimization for emerging 5G and 6G infrastructures.

topics.name: High-speed packet processing/forwarding
topics.description: We develop high-performance networking technologies based on programmable data planes, eBPF/XDP, DPDK, SmartNICs, and hardware accelerators. Our research focuses on scalable packet processing frameworks, in-network computing, and low-latency forwarding across cloud and edge infrastructures.

topics.name: Edge/cloud computing
topics.description: We investigate distributed computing systems spanning cloud, edge, and IoT environments. Research includes workload orchestration, resource scheduling, virtualization, serverless computing, and AI-driven management of applications operating across the computing continuum.

topics.name: Network security analysis, verification and monitoring
topics.description: We develop formal and automated techniques to detect vulnerabilities, verify security configurations, and monitor network traffic. Research includes traffic flow modelling, firewall anomaly detection, formal verification of cryptographic handshake protocols, and security policy synthesis.

topics.name: Software-based network infrastructures and services
topics.description: We study software-defined and virtualized network infrastructures, including SDN, NFV, cloud-native networking, and programmable networks. Our work focuses on network orchestration, service deployment, intent-based management, and automation of network services across distributed infrastructures.

topics.name: Network security automation
topics.description: We investigate autonomous and closed-loop approaches to cybersecurity management, including automated attack detection, firewall reconfiguration, and cyber-resilience in complex cloud and edge environments. Recent work focuses on integrating AI-driven decision making into security orchestration frameworks.
